annotation.title_clean: Humanity at the Crossroads: Autonomous Weapons Systems and the Challenge of Regulation – Chair's Summary
annotation.title_en: Humanity at the Crossroads: Autonomous Weapons Systems and the Challenge of Regulation – Chair's Summary
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Austria, Federal Ministry for European and International Affairs (Conference Chair)
annotation.venue: Vienna Conference on Autonomous Weapons Systems
annotation.summary_en: Chair's Summary of the April 2024 Vienna conference on autonomous weapons systems, attended by 144 States. It calls for a two-tier approach, prohibiting AWS that violate international law or ethics and regulating the rest, and urges negotiation of an international legal instrument by 2026. It stresses human control, accountability and dignity.
key_provisions_or_claims: Strong convergence on a two-tier approach: prohibit unacceptable AWS, regulate all others.
Supports UNSG and ICRC call to conclude an international legal instrument by 2026.
Accountability cannot be transferred to machines; meaningful human control must prevail over use of force.
Concerns about bias, human dignity, proliferation to non-state actors and escalation risks.
Summary to be submitted to the UN Secretary-General for the report under the 2023 UNGA resolution.
